8aa5672156.why: VSHUFPS with immediates 0x88 and 0xdd directly produces the even- and odd-dword groups formed by the initial shuffles and qword unpacks. This preserves the full YMM results, including ymm4 and ymm5, while eliminating four instructions.

cdb1f4a31f.why: The two integer multiply-and-round stages, coefficient store, counter update, and saturating word broadcast all contribute to required results and have no shorter equivalent identified within AVX2.

5f38cd1252.why: The two independently addressed loads and stores, distinct saturation operations, pointer update, and flag-producing counter update leave no redundant instruction.

a12929903c.why: The word, dword, and 128-bit interleaving stages are needed to produce the required transpose, including the preserved intermediate in ymm4.

2353c90e5e.why: All eight dword additions and arithmetic shifts produce required outputs, and AVX2 has no fused operation for these arbitrary dword operands.

0510006e7e.why: The shared increment, eight wrapping dword butterfly results, and arithmetic shifts cannot use byte or word averaging without changing results for arbitrary dword inputs.

6fd3c272c6.why: Every biased dword sum or difference and subsequent shift is required, as is the updated bias in ymm8, with no applicable AVX2 fusion.

6cc959c0f1.why: All eight shifted results and the unshifted final values in ymm8 and ymm10 must be preserved, leaving no removable arithmetic or shift.

c5d3ba7538.why: The two bias constructions feed distinct dword calculations and shifts, and their final register values are also required, so no instruction is redundant.

1eb92d5968.why: Each required wrapping dword butterfly result must be clamped against two arbitrary vector bounds, which AVX2 cannot combine into a single saturation instruction.

8f0d18e78a.why: The required scalar result retains both integer rounding stages, and the coefficient store, counter update, and saturating word broadcast offer no instruction-count reduction within AVX2.
